items.excerpt: Artlist sold filmmakers a year of "unlimited" access to ByteDance's Seedance 2.5 video model for $500, then pulled the unlimited tier within days and swapped it for a modest credit allowance. CineD's breakdown shows the per-second inference economics made the offer impossible from day one — a warning about how gen-video pricing is being marketed to creators.

Dalet launched cloud-native solution suites on its Flex platform with preconfigured workflows and agentic AI built in. The suites center on Dalia, a media-aware AI assistant that lets teams search video libraries, enrich metadata and trigger post/archive workflows through natural language.

ActionVFX launched an online 'VFX for Filmmakers' course aimed at directors and producers who aren't VFX artists, built around After Effects and Photoshop. Its "Modern AI Integration" module teaches depth-map generation, AI-assisted rotoscoping, content-aware fill and LLM-assisted troubleshooting as standard craft steps.

NVIDIA released a Synthetic Video Detector NIM microservice that flags AI-generated footage with up to 92% accuracy on uncompressed material, processing 1080p in 22ms on RTX systems. It is pitched at newsrooms and post teams that now need a provenance check inside the ingest pipeline.

The expanded 2026 AI Creative Summit lands at BFI Southbank on November 11 with three streams covering production workflows, rights and responsible AI, and the skills gap. The programme signals where UK film and TV craft training is being redirected as gen-AI tools move into normal post pipelines.
